script_nghe: So how many countries have you been to? … Eleven now. Twelve if you count changing planes, but I don’t. … Which was your favourite? … Peru, without any doubt. … Is there anything you’ve never tried? … I’ve never been skiing. I’ve always meant to. … What’s the longest trip you’ve taken? … Four months, backpacking. … And what’s next? … Iceland, hopefully in March.

**TRAVEL SURVEY**

- Countries visited so far: **1** ____________
- Favourite country: **2** ____________
- Has never tried: **3** ____________
- Longest trip: **4** ____________ months
- Next destination: **5** ____________

> **Learning by failing**
> 
> Most people assume that the best way to learn a skill is to practise it correctly from the start. A series of studies in the last fifteen years has suggested something less comfortable: learners who make mistakes early, and are then corrected, often outperform those who are guided carefully towards the right answer.
> 
> In one experiment, two groups were given the same set of problems. The first group received clear instructions before attempting them. The second was allowed to struggle for twenty minutes with no help, and only then received the explanation. On the immediate test, the first group performed better. A week later, the second group scored considerably higher.
> 
> Researchers describe this as “productive failure”. The struggle appears to prepare the mind for the explanation, so that the correct method is understood rather than simply copied. The approach has obvious limits — it works poorly where mistakes are dangerous or expensive — but in ordinary classroom learning, the evidence has been consistent.

**True / False / Not Given (6–8):**
6. The group given instructions first did better on the immediate test.
7. Productive failure works well in all situations.
8. The studies were conducted mainly in primary schools.

**Hoàn thành câu (9–11):**
9. The second group struggled for ____________ minutes without help.
10. A week later, the ____________ group scored higher.
11. Researchers call this effect ____________.

writing.de_tom_tat: Viết 80–90 từ: 3 điều bạn đã từng làm và 2 điều bạn chưa bao giờ làm.
writing.bai_mau: I have travelled to five countries in Asia, and I have worked for three different companies. I have also built several small programs to automate my work, which I am quite proud of. On the other hand, there are things I have never done. I have never lived abroad for more than a month, although I would like to. I have never learned to swim properly either, which is something I should probably fix.

cham_diem.vi_sao: have travelled · have worked · have built (bất quy tắc) · have never lived · have never learned. Năm lần đều đúng dạng V3.
never đứng giữa have và V3: have never lived. Không dùng ever trong câu khẳng định.
3 điều đã làm · 2 điều chưa bao giờ làm, có bình luận thêm.

dang_hoc: Hiện tại hoàn thành nói về trải nghiệm không nêu thời điểm. Nêu thời điểm cụ thể thì phải dùng quá khứ đơn.
Vị trí never: giữa have và V3 — I have never been. Không phải "I never have been".
"either" ở cuối câu phủ định = cũng không. Câu khẳng định thì dùng "too".
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ I have never went there → ✅ I have never been there
❌ I have travelled there last year → ✅ I travelled there last year (có thời điểm thì dùng quá khứ đơn)
❌ I have not learned to swim too → ✅ …either

speaking.de_tom_tat: Have you ever travelled abroad? / What's something you've never done but want to? / Have you ever changed career?

cau_tra_loi.mau: Yes, several times. I've been to Thailand, Singapore and Japan. Japan was the most memorable — I went there in 2019.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Trả lời hiện tại hoàn thành trước (I've been), rồi chuyển sang quá khứ đơn khi nêu thời điểm (I went in 2019). Đúng luật.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: What's something you've never done but want to?
cau_tra_loi.mau: I've never lived abroad for a long period. I'd like to work overseas for a year or two, mainly to improve my English and see how things are done elsewhere.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "I've never… but I'd like to" — công thức trả lời cho mọi câu hỏi dạng này.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Not completely, no. I've stayed in e-commerce, but my role has changed a lot. I started in content and I've moved gradually towards data and automation.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "Not completely" là cách trả lời tinh tế hơn "no" — rồi giải thích phần nào có thay đổi.

cham_diem.vi_sao: I've been · I've never lived · I've stayed · has changed · I've moved.

cham_diem.tieu_chi: Chuyển đúng sang quá khứ khi có mốc (1đ)

cham_diem.vi_sao: I've /aɪv/ đọc liền một âm. been /biːn/ chứ không /bɪn/.

meo_noi: Rút gọn khi nói: I've, you've, he's been — người bản xứ hầu như luôn rút gọn.
Câu hỏi "Have you ever…?" thì trả lời "Yes, I have" / "No, I haven't" — không phải "Yes, I did".
